name: The Plane Tree of Fontenay Abbey

location.address: Abbaye de Fontenay, 21500 Marmagne, Cote-d'Or, Burgundy
location.neighbourhood: Grands Jardins (formal gardens) courtyard, Abbaye de Fontenay

access: Paid entry: the Abbey of Fontenay (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) charges admission to enter the grounds and gardens where the tree stands.
transport: Nearest station is Montbard (TGV stop), about 6km away; the abbey is not reachable on foot from a town centre and normally needs a short taxi/drive or the seasonal shuttle from Montbard.
story:
A plane tree about forty metres tall stands in the gardens of one of Europe's best-preserved medieval monasteries, and most visitors photograph the cloister instead. The Abbaye de Fontenay's own site gives the planting year as 1780, which makes the tree roughly 245 years old, and that date belongs to this specimen, not borrowed from the garden around it.

Fontenay is a Cistercian abbey and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and almost everyone who comes here comes for the stone: the Romanesque church, the cloister, the forge. The Comité des Parcs et Jardins de France lists its gardens separately, among them a handful of centuries-old trees, and at forty metres the plane is the one that makes you look up.

It went into the ground nine years before the French Revolution began, and it has grown through everything the abbey has been since. The trunk is said to be around six metres round, though that figure comes from photo captions rather than from the abbey itself, so treat it as a rough guide and not a measurement.

Entry to the abbey is paid, and the plane is inside, so this is a tree you see as part of the visit rather than on the way to it. Montbard, the nearest TGV station, is about six kilometres away, and a short taxi ride or the seasonal shuttle covers the rest.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its height, about forty metres, and a trunk said to be some six metres round. It is the plane planted in 1780 in the formal gardens of the Abbaye de Fontenay.
